result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital with a chest infection (pneumonia).
The infection was in the lower part of your right lung (right lower lobe).
The letter calls it community-acquired pneumonia.
Doctors use a score to judge how serious a chest infection is (CURB-65 score).
Your score was 1.
In hospital, you had antibiotics through a drip into a vein for 1 day.
Then you had amoxicillin tablets.
You have had 2 days of antibiotics in hospital.

## What you need to do
1. Take amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days of antibiotics in total.
2. Have a repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks. This is at the Radiology Department. It checks that the infection has cleared.
3. You do not need to book the chest X-ray yourself. A request has already been sent.

## Dates and medicines
Dates:
- 5 October 2026: you went into hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: your last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: your repeat chest X-ray. The letter does not give an exact date.

Medicine:
- Amoxicillin, 500 milligrams.
- Take it 3 times a day (TDS).
- Change: keep taking it for 3 more days.
- Your last dose is on 10 October 2026.

## Questions to ask your doctor
1. How will I find out the date of my chest X-ray?
2. Which antibiotic did I get through the drip?
3. What times of day should I take my amoxicillin?

## When to get urgent help
See your GP (family doctor) or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath
- your fever comes back
- you cough up blood

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
